title: Risk Oversight for Fund and Management Company Boards
summary: An eight-module programme giving fund and management company directors the tools to oversee investment, operational and emerging risks and challenge the risk function.
intro: This training programme equips fund and management company directors to oversee risk with confidence: understanding the risk profile of the funds, testing the risk function and challenging management on the information behind it.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give directors a structured, practical grounding in the risks run by investment funds and their management companies, and in the board's role in setting appetite and overseeing the risk function. Participants leave able to read risk information critically, challenge stress tests and limits, and evidence effective risk oversight to investors, auditors and supervisors.
sections.What It Covers: Risk concepts and risk appetite, the risk function in a management company, investment risk across market, liquidity, counterparty and leverage, operational and outsourcing risk, risk management information and key risk indicators, stress testing and scenario analysis, and emerging risks from AI, cyber, climate and digital assets.
Intended Audience: Independent and non-executive directors of investment funds and fund management companies
Executive directors, conducting officers and designated persons responsible for risk management
Chief risk officers, heads of compliance and company secretaries supporting fund boards
Learning Objectives: Explain inherent and residual risk, risk appetite and the board's role in fund risk oversight
Evaluate the role, resourcing and independence of the management company's risk function
Assess market, liquidity, counterparty, leverage and operational risk across the fund range
Challenge risk management information, key risk indicators and limit breaches
Interrogate stress tests and scenarios and the actions management proposes in response
Design a board risk dashboard and an oversight plan that keeps pace with emerging risks
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day programme or as a series of board briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with fund case studies and a board question set, ending in a dashboard design workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the board's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience as a fund director or in fund management, administration or risk is helpful. No quantitative or technical risk background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Principles for an Effective Risk Appetite Framework (2013)
IOSCO, Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes (2018)
FSB, Revised Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Liquidity Mismatch in Open-Ended Funds (2023)

modules.title: Risk Concepts for Fund Directors
modules.summary: The building blocks of fund risk oversight: how risk is identified, measured and controlled, how inherent and residual risk differ, and how a risk appetite gives the board a basis for challenge.
objectives: Distinguish inherent risk, controls and residual risk in a fund context
Explain how risk appetite, tolerances and limits fit together
Define where risk oversight sits between the fund board and the management company board
syllabus: The risk management cycle: identify, assess, mitigate, monitor and report
Inherent and residual risk, and the quality of controls in between
Risk appetite statements, tolerances and limits for a fund range
Investor protection as the purpose of fund risk oversight

modules.title: The Risk Function in a Management Company
modules.summary: What a permanent risk management function should do, how it is organised and governed, and how the board satisfies itself that it is independent, adequately resourced and listened to.
objectives: Describe the role, scope and outputs of the risk management function
Assess the independence of the function from portfolio management
Evaluate the risk management policy, process and resourcing
syllabus: Risk management policy, process and procedures across the fund range
Functional and hierarchical independence from portfolio management
Resourcing, systems, data and delegation of risk activities
The head of risk's access to the board and private sessions

modules.title: Investment Risk: Market, Liquidity, Counterparty and Leverage
modules.summary: The main investment risks a fund runs, how each is measured and limited, and the questions directors should ask when a strategy, instrument or market environment changes.
objectives: Explain the main measures of market, liquidity, counterparty and leverage risk
Assess whether limits fit each fund's strategy, investors and dealing terms
Challenge management on concentration, correlation and liquidity mismatch
syllabus: Market risk measures: volatility, tracking error, value at risk and their limits
Liquidity risk: asset liquidity, investor profile, dealing terms and management tools
Counterparty and collateral risk in derivatives, financing and securities lending
Leverage measures, internal limits that trigger before a breach and escalation

modules.title: Operational and Outsourcing Risk
modules.summary: How operational risk arises across the fund's delegated operating model, how outsourcing and sub-delegation change the risk profile, and how the board gains assurance that providers are controlled.
objectives: Identify the main sources of operational risk in a delegated fund model
Evaluate outsourcing due diligence, monitoring and exit arrangements
Assess errors, breaches and incidents as evidence of control quality
syllabus: Risk and control self-assessment, risk registers and loss events
Outsourcing, sub-delegation chains and concentration on key providers
Errors, breaches and incidents: root causes and lessons learned
Business continuity, exit plans and substitutability of providers

modules.title: Risk MI and Key Risk Indicators for Boards
modules.summary: The information a board needs to oversee fund risk, how to read risk reports critically, and how to distinguish genuine assurance from volume of data.
objectives: Specify the core risk information set for a fund board
Interpret key risk indicators, trends and breach reports
Identify gaps, stale data and comfort without evidence
syllabus: The core risk information set: profile, appetite, limits, breaches and actions
Leading and lagging indicators, thresholds and trend analysis
Exception reporting, overdue actions and risk acceptances
Common weaknesses in risk reports and what to ask for instead

modules.title: Stress Testing and Scenario Analysis for Funds
modules.summary: How funds are stress tested for market, liquidity and redemption shocks, what good scenario design looks like, and how the board turns results into decisions rather than reassurance.
objectives: Explain historical, hypothetical and reverse stress tests for funds
Challenge the severity, assumptions and plausibility of scenarios
Agree management actions, triggers and the use of liquidity management tools
syllabus: Asset-side and liability-side stress tests, including redemption shocks
Scenario design: severity, correlation breakdown and second-round effects
Reverse stress testing and the question of what would break the fund
Lessons from fund suspensions and stressed market episodes

modules.title: Emerging Risks: AI, Cyber, Climate and Digital Assets
modules.summary: How new technologies and structural trends change the risk profile of funds and managers, and how the board keeps its risk framework current without chasing every headline.
objectives: Recognise the risks from AI, cyber threats, climate change and digital assets
Assess how these risks enter the fund through investments, providers and operations
Build emerging risks into horizon scanning, appetite and board agendas
syllabus: AI in portfolio management and operations: model, data and dependency risk
Cyber threats, ransomware and resilience of the operating chain
Climate and sustainability risks in portfolios and disclosures
Digital assets, tokenised fund units and custody risk

modules.title: Workshop: The Board Risk Dashboard
modules.summary: Brings the programme together as participants design a board risk dashboard and escalation framework for a fund range, and test it against a live scenario.
objectives: Design a board risk dashboard aligned to appetite and limits
Apply escalation triggers and decision rights to a stressed scenario
Produce a board action plan for strengthening risk oversight
syllabus: Selecting indicators, thresholds and reporting frequency
Escalation routes between management, the risk function and the board
Scenario exercise: a liquidity and operational event in a fund range
Workshop: the board's twelve-month risk oversight plan

related.title: Alternative Investments for Fund Directors
related.summary: An eight-module programme explaining hedge fund, private markets, real asset, structured and digital asset strategies to fund directors, with board questions on valuation, liquidity and fees.

related.title: Board Oversight of Fund Operations and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund directors the tools to oversee fund operations and service providers, from NAV production and custody to errors and resilience.

related.title: Fund Board Governance Toolkit: A Risk-Based Oversight Workshop
related.summary: A six-module practical workshop giving fund directors a risk-based governance toolkit, from skills matrices to escalation triggers, and a draft oversight plan for their own board.

related.title: Investment Fund Governance for Directors
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund directors the tools to oversee delegates, manage conflicts, protect investors and evidence effective governance to supervisors.

related.title: Overseeing Regulatory Change: Annual Update for Fund Directors
related.summary: A six-module annual CPD update for fund directors on the year's regulatory developments and on overseeing regulatory change and regulatory risk.

related.title: AI Governance for Boards
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving boards and directors the understanding and tools to govern AI responsibly and evidence sound oversight to regulators.
